series.name: Stories Beyond the Window
series.description: Godzilla, SHŌGUN, Laid-Back Camp, Dragon Ball and Shinkalion: follow familiar stories into the landscapes and towns along Japan’s railways.
series.kicker: From film, drama and manga to places in Japan
series.hook: A familiar story. A different view of Japan.
series.lead: A river from a film. A lake from Rin’s travels. A place where history turned, a town where a manga artist lived, and real bullet trains that transform into robots. Take a story with you, and the journey between Tokyo, Nagoya and Kyoto becomes part of the discovery.
series.afterwordBody: You might step off a train to explore a place from a story, or simply remember it as the landscape passes. Either way, there is more to the journey than getting there.
series.zukanLink: Find the views along your route

godzilla.label: Godzilla
godzilla.title: Godzilla in Tokyo: from city streets to the train window
godzilla.hook: Meet him in the city. Remember the scene on the train.
godzilla.deck: Look up in Shinjuku, find another Godzilla in Hibiya, then watch for the river from Shin Godzilla.
godzilla.route: Shinjuku and Hibiya on foot; the Tama River between Shinagawa and Shin-Yokohama.
godzilla.alt: The Godzilla Head above a building at the end of a street in Shinjuku
godzilla.searchTitle: Walk through Godzilla’s Tokyo | Shinjuku, Hibiya and the Tama River by train
godzilla.searchDescription: Meet Godzilla in Shinjuku and Hibiya, then recall a film scene as you cross the Tama River. A Tokyo detour connecting cinema, city streets and the Shinkansen window.

shogun.label: SHŌGUN
shogun.title: From SHŌGUN to Sekigahara
shogun.hook: A story on screen. A place outside your window.
shogun.deck: From Toranaga to Tokugawa Ieyasu: discover the history behind a landscape on the Tokyo–Kyoto journey.
shogun.route: Between Gifu-Hashima and Maibara by Shinkansen; walk from JR Sekigahara Station.
shogun.alt: Fields, houses and hills around present-day Sekigahara, seen from a Shinkansen
shogun.searchTitle: From SHŌGUN to Sekigahara | A Shinkansen journey from Toranaga to Ieyasu
shogun.searchDescription: Follow Toranaga from FX’s SHŌGUN to his historical inspiration, Tokugawa Ieyasu, and Sekigahara. Discover the history behind the train-window view and a walk from the station.

yurucamp.label: Laid-Back Camp
yurucamp.title: Laid-Back Camp around Lake Hamana
yurucamp.hook: See the lake. Find your own detour.
yurucamp.deck: A sunset at Bentenjima, a station beside the water: turn Rin’s journey into a stop along your own.
yurucamp.route: Lake views between Hamamatsu and Toyohashi; detours to Bentenjima, Sakume and Kanzanji.
yurucamp.alt: The red torii-shaped tower at Bentenjima against a sunset over Lake Hamana
yurucamp.searchTitle: Laid-Back Camp and Lake Hamana | Rin’s stops at Bentenjima and Hamanako-Sakume
yurucamp.searchDescription: Follow Rin and her friends from Laid-Back Camp Season 2 to Lake Hamana. Explore Bentenjima’s sunset, Hamanako-Sakume Station and Kanzanji Onsen, with access tips for your detour.

dragonball.label: Dragon Ball
dragonball.title: Akira Toriyama’s everyday life in Kiyosu
dragonball.hook: The ordinary days behind extraordinary adventures.
dragonball.deck: Daily calls to a Tokyo editor, manuscripts sent by air: the life and work of Dragon Ball’s creator in his hometown.
dragonball.route: A town beside Nagoya, and a connection to remember when Kiyosu Castle passes your window.
dragonball.alt: The exterior of the BIRD STUDIO office in Kiyosu, photographed in November 2025
dragonball.searchTitle: Dragon Ball and Akira Toriyama’s Kiyosu | The everyday life behind the adventures
dragonball.searchDescription: Explore Kiyosu, where Dragon Ball creator Akira Toriyama lived. Calls with his Tokyo editor, manuscripts sent by air and records of his studio reveal the daily life behind the adventures.

shinkalion.label: Shinkalion
shinkalion.title: Shinkalion: Real Japanese Bullet Trains That Transform into Robots
shinkalion.hook: The train outside your window has a story, too.
shinkalion.deck: Meet the real N700A and N700S behind the robots, then spot the railway museums that became fictional secret bases.
shinkalion.route: On the Tokaido Shinkansen between Nagoya and Kyoto; visit SCMAGLEV and Railway Park or Kyoto Railway Museum after getting off.
shinkalion.alt: A white Shinkansen with the N700A logo, lined up at a train depot
shinkalion.searchTitle: Shinkalion and Shinkansen | From the N700A and N700S to railway museums
shinkalion.searchDescription: In Shinkalion, real Japanese bullet trains transform into robots. Follow official N700A and N700S videos and their real-life counterparts to railway museums in Nagoya and Kyoto.
